I read the whole file (lines 1–101) and checked it against the rubric. I did not open any related source files, and I did not check the definitions of mapLaw_comp, wordWalkLaw_eq and the others beyond how this file uses them.

The only repetition I found is in `unitBitStep_law` and `unitJointDraw_law`. Both start with the same step: a `calc` that rewrites `mapLaw u (g ∘ f)` as `mapLaw (mapLaw u f) g` using `(mapLaw_comp _ f g).symm`. Each then closes with one rewrite by a different law lemma (`smallBitProposal_law_decidableEq` in one, `flatUnitWalk_law` in the other). This is a single application of an existing composition lemma followed by a rewrite. It is short routine plumbing, so a shared helper would be a thin wrapper around `mapLaw_comp`. The rubric excludes that.

`flatUnitWalk_law` and `uniform_singleton_joint` use different arguments and different tools, and `unitJointDraw_variation` is a short chain of existing lemmas. None of them repeats nontrivial reasoning in a second proof.

I found no justified finding. The remaining uncertainty is whether other files repeat these arguments, which this single-file review does not cover.
